library_preparation_preflight.summary: FlatGeobuf is a pure binary encode/decode library for geospatial simple features (FlatBuffers-based), operating entirely in-memory/file I/O with no database, network service, or external process involved. Its two real dependencies — com.google.flatbuffers:flatbuffers-java and org.locationtech.jts:jts-core — are central to its public API (HeaderMeta/GeometryConversions return JTS Geometry types directly), so they are ordinary compile-scope POM dependencies, not optional/provided ones. This matches the repo's own precedent: org.orbisgis:h2gis and com.google.flatbuffers:flatbuffers-java are already-supported libraries whose generated tests use JTS classes and the FlatBuffers runtime respectively with no extra testImplementation entries beyond the standard assertj-core — Gradle resolves those transitive dependencies automatically. No Docker image, environment variable, or system property is plausibly needed for round-trip serialize/deserialize tests against this library.
risks: No network access was available in this environment to fetch the actual org.wololo:flatgeobuf:3.29.0 POM from Maven Central, so the scope (compile vs optional) of its jts-core dependency was inferred from API shape and repo precedent (h2gis) rather than confirmed directly. If checkMetadataFiles/compileTestJava fails with 'cannot find symbol: org.locationtech.jts...', add org.locationtech.jts:jts-core as an explicit testImplementation dependency matching the version flatgeobuf itself pulls.
Local Gradle compile/test and Native Image runs remain authoritative; this is a best-effort desk review, not a verified build.
